name: TX-12
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+11 district with a sitting Republican incumbent
Goldman's ~$1.5M cash advantage against a challenger with no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Republican win odds near 95%
No public polling or expert ratings on the race
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: an incumbent in an R+11 district holding a roughly $1.5 million cash edge over a challenger showing no reported fundraising, with markets pricing Republican odds near 95 percent, leaves little evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: A late surge in Democratic fundraising or outside spending, or a sharp shift in the national political environment, would be the most plausible way this race tightens.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Craig Goldman runs for re-election in a district that has leaned about eleven points Republican in recent partisan baselines. He holds a large financial advantage, with nearly $1.9 million raised and about $1.5 million on hand, while Democratic nominee Angela Rodriguez Prilliman shows no reported fundraising. Outside groups have spent modestly to support Goldman and nothing to oppose him.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, candidate resources, and prediction markets, which put Republican odds near 95 percent. Incumbency, the money gap, and the district's partisan lean all point toward a comfortable Republican hold. The main source of uncertainty is the absence of polling rather than any evidence of a competitive race.
